title: I'm Calling It: Bloom Energy's Revenue Guidance Will Keep Surprising Wall Street Through Year-End
author: James Brumley
description: Bloom Energy, a fuel cell manufacturer, has raised its full-year revenue guidance to $3.9-$4.2 billion (up from $3.4-$3.8 billion) driven by surging demand for AI data center power solutions. With Q2 revenue reaching $1.0 billion and expanding partnerships with Oracle and MiTAC, the company is well-positioned to continue delivering positive surprises through year-end as AI infrastructure investments remain robust.

title: Zoom Appoints Former Oracle CFO Jeff Epstein to Board of Directors; Jonathan Chadwick to Retire
author: Not Specified
description: Zoom announced the appointment of Jeff Epstein, former EVP and CFO of Oracle and current Operating Partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, to its Board of Directors effective immediately. Epstein brings extensive financial and strategic leadership experience in B2B software and AI. Jonathan Chadwick will retire from Zoom's board after nearly ten years of service, effective November 19, 2026.

title: Smart Grid Market to Reach $161.15 Billion, at a 16.9% CAGR by 2029 | MarketsandMarkets™
author: Marketsandmarkets
description: The global smart grid market is expected to grow from USD 73.85 billion in 2024 to USD 161.15 billion by 2029, at a CAGR of 16.9%. Growth is driven by renewable energy integration, grid modernization initiatives, increasing electrification, and rising energy demand. North America leads the market, while Asia Pacific is the fastest-growing region.

title: What Is a Small Modular Reactor, and Why Is Big Tech Signing Multi-Decade Deals for Them?
author: Leo Sun
description: Small modular reactors (SMRs) are compact nuclear reactors producing up to 300 MWe per unit, much smaller than conventional plants. Major tech companies including Google, Amazon, and Oracle are signing multi-decade deals for SMR capacity, driven by rising power demands from cloud infrastructure and AI markets. Key SMR producers NuScale, Oklo, and GE Vernova are positioned to benefit from this growing demand.
